mike: Heads up — last night's perf CI produced a 3.2GB .qdrep and blew past artifact limits. We need a new strategy for automated traces: smaller artifacts + per-kernel diffs for regressions. :grimacing:
anya: ugh, yeah. We should capture targeted windows (nvtx) and only upload excerpts for slow requests. full traces can be stored nightly to a separate long-retention bucket. :+1:
jamal: Agree. Two ideas: 1) lightweight nightly full capture (compressed) for diff dashboards. 2) per-change sampled capture when we see latency SLO violations. Keep per-PR capture to NVTX ranges only.
mike: Good. What's the shortest, reliable CI command for producing a trimmed trace?
jamal: Something like this in the perf job (pseudo):
```
# run the workload under nsys and gzip output
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/trace-${BUILDKITE_BUILD_NUMBER}.qdrep --sample=none -- python -m tests.load_warmup_and_run
gzip -9 ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/*.qdrep
aws s3 cp ${ARTIFACT_DIR}/ s3://redwood-ci-perf/traces/${BUILDKITE_BRANCH}/ --recursive --acl private
```
olivia: For diffs we can't rely on .qdrep raw comparisons. We should export a small CSV with per-kernel aggregates: kernel name, total_time_ms, calls, mean_ms, max_ms. Store that next to the perfetto HTML so the dashboard can diff numeric rows easily.
anya: +1. Also add an artifact that lists NVTX ranges with timestamps so we can align runtime events (batch selection, kv-read, kv-apply). That makes it easier to detect where KV cache thrash happened.
jamal: I'll add an extractor script that uses nsys CLI/trace processor to emit kernel CSV and NVTX timeline. Rough sketch:
```
# trace_to_summary.py (very small)
# open trace.qdrep, for each kernel name: sum durations, count
# for NVTX: list <start, end, label>
# write kernel_summary.csv and nvtx_ranges.json
```
mike: Can you post the actual command you plan to call from CI? We'll need a Buildkite step.
jamal: Sure — Buildkite step (draft):
```
steps:
  - label: "perf: collect trace"
    command:
      - "export ARTIFACT_DIR=$BUILDKITE_BUILD_PATH/perf"
      - "mkdir -p $ARTIFACT_DIR"
      - "nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output $ARTIFACT_DIR/trace.qdrep --capture-range=nvtx -- python -m tests.smoke_infer --trace-window"
      - "python tools/trace_to_summary.py $ARTIFACT_DIR/trace.qdrep $ARTIFACT_DIR"
      - "gzip -9 $ARTIFACT_DIR/*.qdrep"
      - "aws s3 cp $ARTIFACT_DIR s3://redwood-ci-perf/traces/$BUILDKITE_COMMIT/ --recursive"
    artifact_paths:
      - "$ARTIFACT_DIR/**/*"
    branches: "master"
    agents: { "queue": "gpu-small" }
```
anya: A few notes: - use --capture-range=nvtx so we only record NVTX-marked periods (reduces size). - make the nvtx windows deterministic for test harnesses (so CI capture is reproducible).
olivia: About retention: nightly full captures -> s3://redwood-ci-perf/nightly/YYYY-MM-DD/commit/. For per-PR captures keep 7 days and only kernel_summary + perfetto HTML. Full qdrep only if a triage run is triggered.
mike: How do we detect regressions automatically? The dashboard will diff kernel_summary.csv between baseline/nightly and current PR?
olivia: Yes. We'll compute delta% for each kernel and highlight >20% regressions in mean or max. Also flag kernel selection changes (e.g., switched from fp16-fused -> int8 fallback) by comparing the set of kernel names and counts.
jamal: For KV cache behavior, we should add NVTX markers around: kv_lookup_start, kv_lookup_end, kv_apply_start, kv_apply_end, and batch_router_start/end. That way the extractor can report KV-hit vs miss windows and correlate with extra memcpy kernels.
anya: I'll add the NVTX macros in runtime:
```
NVTX_PUSH("kv_lookup");
// do kv read
NVTX_POP();
```
mike: Does anybody think CI time will blow up? We only want this on nightly + sampled PRs. No full trace on every commit.
jamal: Agreed. Plan: - nightly full capture (compressed) for retention - PR: only capture NVTX windows if test detects latency > SLO or if a special label `perf/trace` is set on PR - occasional manual triage runs for huge regressions.
dev-tools-bot: [automation note] created branch perf/ci-trace-collector and assigned jamal, anya. CI job template added to internal repo. :robot_face:
olivia: We'll need a small UI change to the diff dashboard: link each kernel row to the perfetto HTML snapshot (open in iframe) and allow side-by-side kernel timelines. That will make root-cause for kernel-selection regressions obvious.
mike: Sounds good. Action items: 1) jamal: implement trace_to_summary + Buildkite step (target EOD). 2) anya: add NVTX markers and push small PR. 3) olivia: wire upload paths + dashboard CSV ingestion. 4) I'll update perf runbook with retention and sampling policy.
anya: I'll do the NVTX PR first thing tomorrow.
jamal: I'll push the CI step branch and a first-pass extractor. Will ping here when ready for review.
ci-bot: buildkite/perf-collection #457 succeeded (artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci-perf/traces/master/1792345678/). :white_check_mark:
mike: thanks all. If we can get kernel_summary diffs by next week we can catch the int8 fallback regression that sneaked in last release. :eyes:"
